subject: chemistry
title: Compounds: Atoms Joined Up
welcome_lead: When elements bond together, brand-new substances are born. Welcome to compounds.
meta_desc: Learn what compounds are and how they differ from elements in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You now understand how chemical bonds create entirely new substances.

concepts.def: Two or more elements chemically joined together.
A force that holds atoms together in a compound.
Symbols and numbers showing atoms in a compound.
A compound of 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen atom.
CO2: 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms joined.
A change that makes new substances with new properties.

walkthroughs.body_html: A compound is formed when two or more different elements are chemically bonded together. The compound has properties different from the elements it is made from.

Hydrogen is an explosive gas. Oxygen helps things burn. Yet bonded together as H₂O, they form water, which puts fires out!

New compound, new properties.

A chemical formula like CO₂ tells you the elements and how many atoms of each. The little number (subscript) comes after the symbol.

CO₂ = 1 carbon atom + 2 oxygen atoms.

options: Two or more different elements chemically joined
A single element
A mixture of two metals
